properties.description:
Fixes `fact:defect-the-launch-wrapper-cannot-see-a-schema-change`, and the investigation found the defect was WIDER than the fact recorded.

⭐ THE FRAMING THAT MATTERS, and it is sharper than 'the hash was incomplete': THIS HASH IS A GATE IN FRONT OF CARGO'S OWN CHANGE DETECTION. When it decides nothing moved, cargo is never invoked, so cargo's `rerun-if-changed` logic never gets to run. Anything the wrapper misses is therefore not merely untracked — it is actively shielded from the mechanism that would have caught it.

TWO OMISSIONS, and the second was not in the original report:

① `schema/*.yaml`, `include_str!`d by reflow2-core (schema.rs:19-38). A schema-only edit left the hash identical, so the wrapper printed 'binary current, skipping build' and served the previous VOCABULARY. Measured 2026-08-16: `describe_schema` answered with the pre-#199 `change_type` enum while main already declared `defect_fix`, and this session nearly recorded the exact fiction #199 had been merged hours earlier to end.

② `getting-started/skills/**/SKILL.md`, embedded by `crates/reflow2-mcp/build.rs`. THIS ONE IS WORSE AND WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL LOOKED FOR: build.rs ALREADY declares `cargo:rerun-if-changed` on the kit (build.rs:29,50), so cargo would have rebuilt correctly on its own. The wrapper defeated a mechanism that was already right. Editing a SKILL.md served the old text with no warning — and skills change far more often than the schema does.

MEASURED, FOUR CASES, each against both the old and new formula:

    schema edit   new MOVED   old NOT MOVED    <- ①
    SKILL.md edit new MOVED   old NOT MOVED    <- ②
    test edit     new NOT     old NOT          <- counterweight
    src edit      new MOVED   old MOVED        <- counterweight

THE TWO COUNTERWEIGHTS ARE THE POINT. Tests stay OUT deliberately — they are separate cargo targets and cannot change the binary this serves, so including them would rebuild on every test edit and train people to distrust the wrapper. And a `src/*.rs` edit still moves both formulas, so nothing that already worked regressed.

📌 ONE-TIME COST, stated so it does not read as a fault: the first launch after this change rebuilds once regardless, because the stored `.reflow2-mcp.srchash` stamp was computed under the old formula and cannot match the new one. Observed and expected; stable from the second launch.

NOT A REGISTERED ARTIFACT and nothing tests it — which is why the four-case measurement is recorded here rather than as a Verification. CONSUMERS ARE UNAFFECTED throughout: they run an installed release binary, never this wrapper.

NOT FIXED: the wrapper still cannot notice that a RUNNING server has gone stale — it only decides what to build at launch. A session whose server started before a schema change still needs `--stop-shared`, and nothing tells it so.
properties.name: The launch wrapper's hash covers the schema and the skills — the two trees compiled into the binary from outside src/, both of which it was silently blind to
